data.title: Fangzhou and Baiyunshan Pharmaceutical Launch AI-Powered Chronic Disease Management Initiative
data.description:
GUANGZHOU, China, Nov. 19, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Fangzhou Inc. (“Fangzhou” or the “Company”) HKEX:06086, a leading provider of AI‑driven Internet healthcare solutions, announced a strategic partnership with Baiyunshan Pharmaceutical General Factory (“Baiyunshan Pharmaceutical”) at its 2026 Double 12 Partner Conference in Guangzhou, as the companies seek to expand AI-powered healthcare services and develop new digital marketing solutions.

Fangzhou and Baiyunshan Pharmaceutical Launch AI-Powered Chronic Disease Management Initiative

The conference brought together industry experts, pharmaceutical partners and healthcare professionals to explore opportunities in AI-powered digital marketing and full-lifecycle health management.

At the conference, Fangzhou presented the latest developments in its “AI + Chronic Disease Services” strategy. The Company has expanded AI applications across health monitoring, patient follow-up and health education, while upgrading its AI Health Manager, AI Medication Assistant and AI pre-consultation tools to further enhance services for patients and physicians.

“Digital transformation is not simply about upgrading individual tools, but about reshaping how healthcare services are delivered,” said Mr. Wang Haijiao, Executive Director and Chief Executive Officer of Fangzhou. “Our focus is on leveraging our medical resources and technology capabilities to deliver practical, high-quality care solutions for our users.”

Wang added that Fangzhou plans to work more closely with partners to develop integrated services covering online health assessments, one-on-one follow-up support, professional health guidance and prescription fulfillment.

Baiyunshan Pharmaceutical is an established Chinese drug manufacturer with businesses spanning antibiotics, reproductive health and traditional Chinese medicine, as well as development pipeline of innovative oncology treatments. The partnership will focus on developing a digital marketing ecosystem and exploring new business models by combining Fangzhou's AI-powered healthcare capabilities and broad service reach with Baiyunshan Pharmaceutical's product portfolio and industry expertise. Wang added that the companies hope to improve access to medical innovations while extending healthcare services across the patient lifecycle.

Kong Jian, Party Secretary and Chairman of Baiyunshan Pharmaceutical, said the two companies have built a strong foundation through more than a decade of collaboration. He described the new agreement as an opportunity to establish a model for AI-powered chronic disease services and jointly develop digital marketing capabilities that make quality healthcare more accessible.

Looking ahead, Fangzhou will continue strengthening its position as a “full-lifecycle personal health service partner,” expanding its AI-powered chronic disease services and working with pharmaceutical companies and other industry partners to improve healthcare accessibility and efficiency across China.

About Fangzhou Inc.

Fangzhou Inc. HKEX:06086 is China’s leading online chronic disease management platform, serving 59.8 million registered users and 282,000 physicians (as of June 30, 2026). The Company specializes in delivering tailored medical care and AI‑enabled precision medicine solutions. For more information, visit https://investors.jianke.com.

data.title: Mahanadi Coalfields raises ₹2,295 crore from anchor investors ahead of IPO
data.description:
Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd, a subsidiary of Coal India, on Wednesday raised Rs 2,295 crore from anchor investors ahead of its initial public offering, which opens for subscription on Thursday.

The company has allotted 16,87,68,255 equity shares at Rs 136 apiece to anchor investors, comprising 53 funds, according to a circular uploaded on the stock exchanges.

Investors participating in the anchor round include Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC), which was allotted shares worth Rs 568 crore and Nippon Life India Trustee, which received shares worth nearly Rs 500 crore across its two schemes.

Other investors included Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, Invesco Mutual Fund, Tata AIG General Insurance Company, Tata Mutual Fund, HDFC Mutual Fund, ICICI Prudential Mutual Fund, Aditya Birla Sun Life Mutual Fund, Motilal Oswal Mutual Fund, Edelweiss Mutual Fund, Axis Mutual Fund, General Insurance Corporation of India, Bajaj Life Insurance and SBI General Insurance.

Domestic mutual funds get 53% of anchor allocation

Domestic mutual funds were allotted 8.95 crore shares, accounting for 53 per cent of the total anchor allocation. The shares were allocated to 11 mutual funds through 29 schemes.

Mahanadi Coalfields has fixed a price band of Rs 129-136 per share, valuing the company at a little over Rs 90,000 crore. The issue will close on November 23.

The Rs 8,981-crore Initial Public Offering (IPO), entirely an offer for sale, will see promoter Coal India divest a 10 per cent stake through the sale of up to 66.18 crore equity shares.

Entire IPO proceeds to go to Coal India

Since the issue comprises only an offer for sale, MCL will not receive any proceeds from the IPO. The entire proceeds will go to Coal India, the selling shareholder.

The proposed listing is part of Coal India’s broader plan to unlock value from its subsidiaries through the capital markets.

MCL will become the third Coal India subsidiary to tap the public markets this year. Coal India has already listed Bharat Coking Coal Ltd in January, while the IPO of Central Mine Planning & Design Institute Ltd opened in March.

The company’s shares are likely to be listed on the BSE and the NSE on November 27.

MCL accounts for 22.4% of India’s non-coking coal production

Incorporated in 1992, MCL produced 218.31 million tonnes of coal in FY26, accounting for around 22.4 per cent of India’s total non-coking coal production, according to the Crisil report cited in the offer documents.

It is also the largest coal-producing subsidiary of Coal India, contributing over 28 per cent to the state-owned company’s total coal production in FY26.

Coal India accounts for more than 80 per cent of the country’s domestic coal output.

SBI Capital Markets, Axis Capital, BOB Capital Markets, IDBI Capital Markets & Securities and IIFL Capital Services are the book-running lead managers to the issue, while KFin Technologies is the registrar.

data.title: a2 Milk says China-label offtake recovers to 50% of distribution levels
data.description:
New Zealand's a2 Milk said on Thursday that estimated offtake for its China-label infant milk formula (IMF) had recovered to around 50% of pre-disruption levels from roughly 40% in August.

The dairy giant said in April that in-market supply of China-label IMF had been hit by low inventory levels, strong demand and higher freight costs due to the conflict in the Middle East.

  • a2 Milk expects China-label and English-label IMF sales to gradually recover in fiscal 2027, supported by new product launches, among others

  • "We are supporting the trade ecosystem and have intentionally constrained distribution to around two thirds of prior levels to support rate of sale at retail," Managing Director and CEO David Bortolussi said

  • The firm will ramp up its marketing investment in the first half, with group revenue and operating earnings expected to be heavily weighted towards the second half of the year

  • Supply-chain disruptions in the China-label business cut fiscal 2026 revenue from IMF sales by 14%, while group annual net profit fell 44% to NZ$113.6 million ($62.36 million), below market estimates

  • a2 Milk maintained its fiscal 2027 outlook of mid-single-digit revenue growth but now expects first-half revenue to be slightly lower than the same period in 2026, after forecasting in August that it would be broadly in line

  • Citi said in a note that the improvement in China-label sales had not generated enough momentum to maintain a2 Milk's previous first-half revenue forecast, pointing to a slower-than-expected recovery

  • Shares fell as much as 10.3% to NZ$7.96, their biggest intraday decline since early May

($1 = 1.8218 New Zealand dollars)

data.title: BOJ's Ueda Reaffirms Readiness to Keep Raising Rates
data.description:
By Megumi Fujikawa

TOKYO--Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda again reiterated that he is prepared to tighten monetary policy further, reinforcing market views that another interest-rate hike could come as soon as December.

Speaking to a parliamentary committee on Thursday, Ueda said it is important to keep underlying consumer inflation anchored around 2% so that it doesn't overshoot the central bank's 2% target and hurt the economy.

"The bank will continue to raise the policy interest rate and adjust the degree of monetary accommodation, in response to developments in economic activity and prices as well as financial conditions," he said.

Ueda warned that one measure of underlying inflation--consumer prices excluding fresh food--is likely to accelerate clearly above 2% as firms pass on higher labor costs, oil remains expensive and the yen's weakness persists. Surging global demand related to the artificial-intelligence buildout adds another inflationary impulse.

In September, that gauge of underlying inflation accelerated to 2.1% year-on-year from August's 1.7%. Economists polled by data provider Quick expect October data due Friday to show a further rise to 2.3%.

The BOJ said last month that underlying inflation had reached its 2% target for the first time since the goal was introduced in 2013.

Write to Megumi Fujikawa at megumi.fujikawa@wsj.com

data.title: Indonesian fire emissions third highest on record this year, EU's Copernicus says
data.description:
This year's fires in Indonesia produced nearly 200 million metric tons of carbon emissions by November 15, the European Union's climate monitoring service said on Thursday, the third-highest annual volume on record.

  • The archipelago has suffered its worst wildfire season in years, driven by excessively dry super-El Niño weather conditions and warmer temperatures, as well as extensive land clearing

  • Total fire emissions fell short of the record of nearly 400 million tons in 2015 and were also slightly lower than in 2006, another strong El Niño year, according to the EU's Copernicus Atmosphere Monitoring Service (CAMS), which tracks fire emission records dating back to 2003

  • This year's fire emissions were the equivalent of more than a fifth of Indonesia's total carbon footprint in 2025, with the country's energy consumption and industry responsible for an estimated 960 million tons of CO2 last year, according to the Statistical Review of World Energy

  • Emissions generated by Indonesia's fires were also around the same as the entire energy and industrial carbon footprint of Pakistan last year

  • CAMS data showed that nearly 8.9 million hectares (22 million acres) of land could have been damaged by fire in Indonesia this year, 4.7% of its total area, significantly higher than the 2012 to 2025 average of 1.9%.

  • The figure is significantly higher than the 2.9-million-hectare estimate for January to October provided last week by geomonitoring platform Nusantara Atlas, which uses a more conservative methodology

  • Though El Niño-driven drought was a decisive factor in this year's fires, experts have also emphasised the role played by climate change in driving up temperatures

  • Poor land management and the excessive draining of peatland to make way for palm oil or pulpwood concessions have also made Indonesia more vulnerable to fire

data.title: Defence Stocks: HAL, BEL, BDL, peers in the spotlight after ministry seeks 20% hike in FY28 capex
data.description:
Shares of defence companies, including Hindustan Aeronautics Ltd. (HAL), Bharat Electronics Ltd. (BEL), and Bharat Dynamics Ltd. (BDL), will be in focus on Thursday, November 19, after the Defence Ministry reportedly sought a 20% increase in capital expenditure for FY28, potentially to fund major acquisitions.

The proposed spending push could support big-ticket procurement programmes, including the acquisition of 114 Rafale fighter jets and six advanced conventional submarines equipped with Air-Independent Propulsion (AIP) under Project 75I.

India's defence capital expenditure allocation for FY27 stood at ₹2.19 lakh crore, marking a 22% increase over the FY26 Budget estimate of ₹1.8 lakh crore.

The Defence Ministry has signed contracts worth around ₹80,000 crore so far in the current financial year.

Meanwhile, India's defence exports have risen sharply from ₹600 crore to a record ₹38,000 crore. The government's target of achieving ₹50,000 crore in defence exports by 2029 could potentially be met ahead of schedule.

Other key development

The government is expected to announce the winner of the competition to develop prototypes of the Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA), India's proposed fifth-generation stealth fighter.

Defence Minister Rajnath Singh has said the selected entity will be a private-sector company or a private-sector-led consortium, potentially involving a public-sector partner.

According to media reports, three groups are competing for the estimated ₹15,000-crore programme:

- Tata Advanced Systems

- Larsen & Toubro (L&T), in partnership with Bharat Electronics Ltd. (BEL) and Dynamatic Technologies

- Bharat Forge, in partnership with BEML and Data Patterns

data.title: dorsaVi Opens New International Sales Channel with LuxingSport French Distribution Deal
data.description:
dorsaVi Limited has signed its first French distribution agreement, opening a new route to overseas customers for its movement-analysis technology without the expense of building a local sales team.

France-based LuxingSport will introduce the Australian technology developer’s products to professional sporting organisations, physiotherapists, and research groups through its existing sales network.

The deal marks the first step in a wider distributor-led expansion across Europe and Asia, with dorsaVi to continue selling directly to customers in Australia and the US.

Initial French sales activity is expected to start in November and December, after which the partners plan a broader market-development campaign during 2027.

French Partner with Reach

Headed by Laurent Massias, LuxingSport already works with the kinds of specialist customers dorsaVi wants to reach.

Massias approached the business several months ago after examining its range of wearable sensors and software used to measure and assess human movement.

Those products have been deployed in elite sport, clinical treatment, and workplace settings, giving dorsaVi an established platform to take into new territories.

The company’s technology has previously been used by organisations including Boeing, Caterpillar, and Medtronic, as well as by professional sporting bodies, existing relationships that are unrelated to the French agreement.

Lite International Expansion

Rather than recruiting and managing a separate salesforce in France, dorsaVi will draw on LuxingSport’s customer relationships and local market knowledge, leaving the company free to concentrate more of its resources on product development, training, and technical support as distributors seek customers on the ground.

“Rather than building large sales teams in every new jurisdiction, we see an opportunity to work with capable distributors who understand their customers and already have established routes to market,” group chief executive officer Mathew Regan said.

“LuxingSport is an encouraging first partner for this approach—its experience in elite sport, physiotherapy, and research aligns well with the customers and applications for which dorsaVi’s products have been developed.”

dorsaVi is looking beyond France to other European countries, Japan, and selected Asian markets where medical technology, rehabilitation, and sports-performance businesses have established distribution networks.

Any additional territories will be considered against customer demand, regulatory requirements, and the capabilities and commercial terms offered by prospective partners.

Flexible Sales Agreement

The French arrangement is non-exclusive and runs initially for 12 months, with automatic annual renewals unless either party provides 90 days’ notice.

LuxingSport will buy dorsaVi products and subscriptions for resale, paying for accepted orders rather than committing to a fixed volume upfront, with no minimum purchase quantities or compulsory inventory commitments and the value of future sales yet to be established.

dorsaVi plans to support the rollout with partner training and commercial assistance while maintaining its own sales relationships in Australia and the US.

The French launch will sit alongside those established operations, rather than replace the sales activities dorsaVi already maintains in its two core markets.

data.title: Indian rupee's inflow-driven upward momentum faces hawkish Fed headwinds
data.description:
By Nimesh Vora

The Indian rupee is expected to open largely flat on Thursday, with sustained foreign equity inflows cushioning it against dollar strength amid hawkish Federal Reserve signals.

The rupee is expected to open little changed after settling at 93.44 to the dollar on Wednesday. It climbed to 93.2450 during the session, its highest level in nearly seven months, before slipping.

Still, the currency remains on an upward trajectory, bankers said, underpinned by foreign equity inflows and a shift in market positioning, with speculators increasingly reluctant to take on dollar-long bets.

On Wednesday, while the rally in Indian equities lost steam, foreign investors continued to buy, pumping more than $600 million into domestic shares. This takes their net purchases so far this month to nearly $12 billion.

The bias on USD/INR remains on the downside; however, the move is likely to be more of a "incremental" move lower, a currency trader at a bank said.

The rupee has already recovered substantially, and further move higher may come at a measured pace, with intermittent bouts of "consolidation and opportunities", he said.

The rupee's recovery is facing an external headwind as Federal Reserve officials signal that the fight against inflation may require a more aggressive policy response.

Minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, released on Wednesday, showed policymakers increasingly concerned that inflation could prove persistent, with some calling for further tightening.

That hawkish tone was reinforced by Fed Governor Christopher Waller, who said the central bank should either deliver a 50-basis-point rate hike in December or signal a faster pace of increases in 2027.

The remarks are likely to keep the dollar supported, with the currency already trading near a one-and-a-half-year high.

Danske Bank has added a January rate hike to its Federal Reserve outlook, and now expects three further 25-basis-point increases in December, January and March, taking the fed funds rate to 4.50%-4.75%, where it sees rates remaining through the rest of 2027.

data.title: Indonesia's Aneka Petroindo signs deal to buy Vivo petrol stations
data.description:
Indonesia's PT Aneka Petroindo Raya, the operator of BP-AKR petrol stations in the country, has signed a deal to buy a 90% stake in PT Vivo Energy Indonesia, an affiliate of the Swiss-based Vitol Group.

  • The remaining 10% of PT Vivo Energy Indonesia will be acquired by a non-affiliate firm, Aneka Petroindo Raya (APR) said in a statement

  • APR will integrate Vivo's 47 locations into its petrol station operations and plans to rebrand them as BP-AKR stations, according to the statement issued late on Wednesday

  • The overall transaction was valued at $15.5 million, according to a stock exchange filing by APR's parent company AKR Corporindo

  • APR currently operates 75 BP-AKR petrol stations on Java island

  • BP sold its 49.9% stake in APR earlier this month to AKR Corporindo, making AKR the sole owner of the operator

  • The company will continue to use the BP-AKR brand for its petrol stations

  • Indonesia's energy ministry tightened direct fuel imports by private firms last year, resulting in shortages at private fuel stations, including those operated by BP and Shell

  • Shell announced in October that it had completed the transfer of ownership of its Indonesian petrol station business to the SEFAS Group

data.title: Uber Co-Founder Kalanick Teases Protest at Nvidia as Calls for Huang's Return Continue — WSJ
data.description:
By Angel Au-Yeung

Uber co-founder Travis Kalanick walked on stage at an investor conference in Austin, Texas, wearing a black leather jacket. Next to him was Antonio Gracias, close friend and longtime investor of Elon Musk — also in a black leather jacket.

"Yours looks a lot like Jensen's," said Gracias, referring to Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang, who had made a black leather jacket his uniform and was ousted last week as chief executive of the chip maker.

"Yeah, we gotta bring Jensen back," said Kalanick.

Calls from Silicon Valley's elite for Huang's reinstatement continued to reverberate Wednesday, even after Nvidia's board chairman declared that the company has no intention of bringing him back. Huang stepped down last week following reports of affairs with two women, one of whom U.S. officials had suspected was passing information to Chinese intelligence during their relationship.

While on stage at the TomorrowX Summit, Kalanick said he would show up at Nvidia's offices "with a wafer encrusted megaphone" to lead employees on a walkout. "Let's fight for what's right and give it a best shot," he said. "We don't have control of the outcome, but let's f — ing fight."

Kalanick compared Huang's saga to his own fight to remain CEO of Uber before resigning under pressure in 2017. Kalanick couldn't immediately be reached for comment.

Huang's supporters have argued that the former CEO is pro-American and essential to ensuring that the U.S. has a thriving open-source AI ecosystem. They have questioned why he was forced out before an investigation announced by the board delivered its findings.

At the New York Times DealBook Summit, also on Wednesday, the technorati took turns praising Huang.

Musk compared Huang's ouster to "kicking Michael Jordan off your team when you're on a winning streak." The billionaire, who appeared remotely from China, also reiterated past comments he wrote on X that he would hire Huang.

Greg Brockman, president of OpenAI, described Huang as "singular" while OpenAI chief executive Sam Altman said it was "hard to imagine the AI industry without Jensen." Palmer Luckey, founder of Anduril Industries, said that "nobody can take Jensen's place in this critical juncture."

"Has NVIDIA's Board lost perspective?" wrote Ron Conway, venture capitalist and founder of SV Angels, on X. "The Board prejudged him even before their own internal investigation was completed. Why push out a visionary American founder?"

Bill Ackman, founder of Pershing Square, also took to X to lambaste Nvidia's directors. "The board's conduct here is shocking for a company of this scale and importance to our country and the world at large, particularly at this moment in history," he wrote on X.

In Huang's first public remarks on Tuesday since he stepped down, he said he would be willing to return to Nvidia as chief executive if the board believes "my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America."

Write to Angel Au-Yeung at angel.au-yeung@wsj.com

data.title: Gold recovers from over one-year low as markets assess Fed rate outlook
data.description:
Key points:
  • Traders price in 90% chance of a 25-bp Fed hike in December
  • Global Platinum market to swing back to deficit next year
  • Break below $3,800 risks reinforcing bearish sentiment- OCBC analysts

By Sukanya Mitra

Gold prices rose on Thursday after hitting a more than one-year low in the previous session, as investors looked to Federal Reserve commentary for clues on the US interest-rate outlook.

Spot gold was up 0.6% at $3,743.26 per ounce, as of 0240 GMT, after hitting its lowest level since September 2025 in the previous session. U.S. gold futures for December delivery gained 0.1% to $3,744.30.

"It's (Gold) making a mild attempt to lift itself from its 13-month low, but this is more likely to be profit-taking from bears over any fundamental catalyst," said Matt Simpson, senior market analyst at StoneX.

Fed officials saw a growing risk last month that they might need to intensify their efforts to control inflation, even as they agreed to keep interest rates steady for the moment, the minutes of their October 27-28 showed on Wednesday.

Fed Governor Michael Barr said he's likely to be on board with tighter monetary policy in an economy still beset by inflation pressures.

Additionally, Fed Governor Christopher Waller said the US central bank needs to get more aggressive in its response to inflation, and either approve a half-point hike at the December meeting or communicate a faster pace of interest rate increases in 2027.

Markets see a 90% chance of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, while the probability of a larger 50-basis-point move is priced at 10%, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

Higher interest rates increase the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding bullion, reducing its appeal to investors.

"The break below $3,800 risks reinforcing bearish sentiment. Buying interest remains subdued, while the continued decline raises the risk of further liquidation," analysts at OCBC said in a note.

Meanwhile, the global platinum market will swing back to deficit next year due to higher bar and coin demand and smaller outflows from platinum-backed exchange-traded funds, the World Platinum Investment Council said on Wednesday.

Spot silver was up 0.6% at $45.27 per ounce, platinum edged 0.1% higher to $1,373.35 and palladium gained 0.7% to $954.60.
